newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen pares losses after BOJ operation.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen pares losses after BOJ operation.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE was slightly down in early trade on Wednesday, but pared part of its initial losses after the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) money market operation, which was more accommodative than expected, traders said.
The December stood at 99.12 as of 9.40 a.m. (0040 GMT), down 0.02 from Tuesday.

The key contract fell as low as 99.10 shortly after the open on remarks by a key Finance Ministry official to a newspaper which suggested long-term interest rates could rise once people realise that the Japanese economy is not that bad.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, was quoted by Wednesday's Yomiuri Shimbun as saying that Japan's long-term interest rates were at record low levels, but could rise once people realise that the Japanese economy is not that bad.

"Position-squaring selling emerged from the start of the trade following Sakakibara's comments. Some people were disappointed that euroyen futures did not benefit much from the recent rally in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures," said a city bank trader.
Euroyen futures bounced back from their earlier lows following the BOJ's 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) money market operation.
The BOJ injected 100 billion yen into the money market on Wednesday morning, leaving a surplus of about 300 billion yen.
Market participants had expected the central bank to leave a surplus of about 100 billion yen by draining 100 billion yen today, traders said.
The unsecured overnight call rate fell to 0.44 percent after the BOJ operation, down sharply from Tuesday's weighted average of 0.51 percent.
About 100 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposits (CDs) was issued at 0.55 percent on Wednesday morning, traders said. They were issued at 0.55 and 0.54 percent on Tuesday.
